_comment: Packages the weekly Dependency Update Agent must NOT bump, with the reason and
the story that owns lifting the hold. Read by .github/workflows/dependency-update.yml.
A hold exists because the agent installs every non-breaking update as ONE batch and
gates the batch on `npm run validate && npm run build`. One package that fails the
gate therefore blocks the other sixty. That is not hypothetical: every run from
2026-07-13 to 2026-09-14 failed on @supabase/supabase-js alone and opened zero PRs
(WEB-QUAL-011). That hold was lifted on 2026-09-19 by WEB-QUAL-015, which fixed the
fourteen files 2.85+ newly rejected - nine of them live defects.
A hold is a deferral, not a decision. Each entry names an owning story and a
`firstBadVersion` is the earliest version known to fail the gate - the hold blocks
that version and everything after it, so patch releases below it still land.

holds.name: three
holds.reason: 0.160 -> 0.186 is a breaking change in three's 0.x scheme, and @react-three/fiber is pinned at 8.16.8 whose peer range predates it. three moves with the fiber 8 -> 9 major, not on its own.

holds.name: @types/dompurify
holds.reason: npm's `latest` for this package is 3.0.5, BELOW the installed 3.2.0 - the 3.0.5 publish is the deprecation stub that redirects to dompurify's own bundled types. Bumping to `latest` is a downgrade.
